title: Plan C: AI Avatar Presenters
summary: Pick a tool → prepare the avatar → write the script → one-click generation → post-process & publish
scenario: Best for batch talking-head videos without showing your own face, corporate training, and multilingual export. Core loop: avatar + script + one-click generation.

steps.title: Pick a tool
steps.detail: Tencent Zhiying (most China-friendly, strong Chinese, generous free credits); HeyGen (best quality, 95%+ lip sync, ~$1-2/min); D-ID (cheap and sufficient, ~$0.3-0.7/min). Advanced: record 2-5 minutes of yourself and train an 'Instant Avatar' in HeyGen to clone your own presenter.

steps.title: Prepare the avatar
steps.detail: Start with a platform preset, or generate a custom presenter from a headshot (even lighting, clean background, ≥720p resolution).

steps.title: Write the talking-head script
steps.detail: 100-300 words, short sentences with plenty of commas. Avatar lip sync is driven entirely by punctuation — the more standard your punctuation, the better the result.

steps.title: Generate and render
steps.detail: Paste the script, pick a voice, submit the render (a 1-minute video takes about 1-2 minutes). Then check lip sync, expression and voice fit.
steps.tips: Play each segment and check the lips; re-render only the sentences that fail rather than restarting the whole video.

steps.title: Post-process and publish
steps.detail: Add captions, BGM and transitions in CapCut, then publish. For multilingual export, use HeyGen's multilingual lip sync to produce every language version from one script.

pitfalls.title: Too few punctuation marks → lips out of sync
pitfalls.detail: Lip sync depends on punctuation. Always split long sentences, add commas, and use periods to make the avatar stop and pause.

pitfalls.title: Free avatars look like 'mannequins'
pitfalls.detail: Free-tier presenters have stiff motion. For real quality, pay for a tier or upload a cloned video of yourself.

pitfalls.title: Licensing and watermarks
pitfalls.detail: Some free tiers watermark output or restrict commercial use. Confirm the license before bulk commercial publishing.
